LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 15.1.1 ORAL REPORTS: NEWS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 15.1: Listening and speaking 15.1.1 Oral Reports: News

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Listening and speaking 15.1.1 Oral Reports: News. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should we use polite language?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use euphemism to show politeness in communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 15.1.1 ORAL REPORTS: NEWS
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Listening and speaking 15.1.1 Oral Reports: News helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 15.1.1 ORAL REPORTS: NEWS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Use euphemism to show politeness in communication

What this means
In this part you learn to use euphemism to show politeness in communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use euphemism to show politeness in communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Listening and speaking 15.1.1 Oral Reports: News”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use euphemism to show politeness in communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Listening and speaking 15.1.1 Oral Reports: News is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Listening and speaking 15.1.1 Oral Reports: News”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: use euphemism to show politeness in communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Listening and speaking 15.1.1 Oral Reports: News to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: use euphemism to show politeness in communication.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Listening and speaking 15.1.1 Oral Reports: News from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Listening and speaking 15.1.1 Oral Reports: News: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Listening and speaking 15.1.1 Oral Reports: News?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we use polite language?
2. Why is it embarrassing to say some words in public?
3. How can we show good citizenship with regards to road safety?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Listening and speaking 15.1.1 Oral Reports: News means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: use euphemism to show politeness in communication.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
